title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 56
paragraphs: He, then, went back to the Athenians. As dawn still found them arguing with one another, Pausanias, who had stayed still throughout all this time, gave the signal and led all the rest away over the low hills, supposing that Amompharetos would not stay behind when the other Lacedaemonians departed — in which he was in fact right. With them went the Tegeans too. Meanwhile the Athenians, following the orders given them, were going in the direction opposite to the Lacedaemonians; for these clung to the hills and the lower slope of Kithairon out of fear of the cavalry, while the Athenians marched below in the direction of the plain.
